newsitem.title: CANADA: Proposed Canada-Chicago gas pipeline 85 pct full.
newsitem.headline: Proposed Canada-Chicago gas pipeline 85 pct full.

text.p: The proposed C$3.6 billion Alliance Pipeline, which would ship natural gas to Chicago from northern Canada, has garnered shipping commitments totalling 1.1 billion cubic feet a day or about 85 percent of its planned capacity, Alliance chief executive Dennis Cornelson said on Tuesday.
The number of unconditional agreements for the 3,000 km pipeline, which have terms of 15 years, represented a strong chance the project would go ahead, Cornelson said.
"I think it's a go -- that's the important thing to note now," he said after a speech to a gas conference.

The backers of the line, which would be the largest planned capital project in Canada, have touted it as a gas transport alternative aimed at offering access to one of North America's richest gas markets at cheaper rates.

A lack of abundant export capacity out of Alberta has often been blamed for Canadian gas prices which have been more than US$1 per million British thermal units under those in such regions as the U.S. Midwest and Gulf Coast.

Alliance would compete with several other pipeline firms which are also in expansion mode, including NOVA Corp, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, Foothills Pipe Lines Ltd, Northern Border Pipeline Co and Natural Gas Pipeline of America.
The competitors have filed interventions to Alliance's application with the FERC, arguing the project will cause a glut of Canadian gas in the U.S. Midwest market.

Cornelson, who pointed out that the only opposition to the project has come from the competitors, said he disagreed with their contention because Chicago was a "market clearing center" with several pipelines that could take gas to growing markets further east.
The Alliance group includes such companies as Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Chevron Corp unit Chevron Canada Resources Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.
The scheduled startup for the project is in late 1999.
The liquids-rich gas pipeline, which is being planned by a consortium of 18 Canadian energy firms, has filed for a capacity of over 1.3 billion cubic feet a day.
Its regulatory application for the U.S. portion is being studied by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

"We're looking to fill up the balance of the capacity. But frankly at 1.1 billion a day, we're at 85 percent of where we need to be and we'll fill that capacity one way or another," Cornelson told reporters.
